claim: *From engineering question to engineering consequence.* Hold the system fixed and change the question, and the useful representation changes with it. The representation determines which analyses become tractable; analysis produces evidence that can inform architecture and design, expose a property for checking, or both. Chapter 3 takes up the separate question of which obligations should be enforced.

topology.description: Question→representation→analysis→evidence; evidence informs design, enforcement, or both.

required_terms: Choose representation Closed state/action space · finite transition system · temporal behavior
Choose analysis appropriate to the property Constraint solving · state exploration · model checking · simulation · static analysis
Inform architecture / design Compare alternatives · revise boundaries Change dependencies · allocate resources
bw_encoding: All stages and both consequence alternatives white; no darker alternative implies priority.
redesign: All stages and both consequence alternatives white; no darker alternative implies priority. Vertical stages and orthogonal shared-rail consequence fork.
alt: An engineering question leads to representation, analysis and interpreted evidence. Evidence then branches to architecture and design decisions or to an obligation deserving enforcement through Alignment, or both. Example representations and analyses illustrate choices rather than a prescribed pairing.

review.reference: current authored SVG (not older D2 receipts)
review.outcome: Representation, design and enforcement distinguished by gray roles; evidence can inform either or both.
review.strict_compile: zero warnings, overfull boxes, missing glyphs or errors

style_review.fill: All stages and both consequence alternatives white; no darker alternative implies priority.
style_review.bold: No bold body or node labels; semantic hierarchy uses placement, spacing and named structure.
style_review.routing: Vertical stages and orthogonal shared-rail consequence fork.
style_review.shape: Ordinary boxes use modest rounded corners; semantic document, state, decision, marker and quantitative shapes retain their roles.
style_review.visual_review: Original source and candidate semantics compared; final-size native render inspected for fill, hierarchy, routes and legibility.
